name: Once Upon a Brand

pick.label: Pick a product
pick.heading: Pick a product and give it a story
lead: Some brands sell a thing. Others sell a story: a founder, a place, a year, a moment that everybody tells again and again, and suddenly a jar of jam costs seven euros.
Choose a completely ordinary product and give it a brand with an origin story. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. *The more boring the product, the better the story has to be.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: Your story doesn’t have to be true, or even possible. This is just for a bit of fun. Some stories would sell in a Mitte concept store, and some only make sense at two in the morning. Both are welcome.

rows: What ordinary thing are you turning into a brand?
Give it a name that already sounds like it has a history.
Who? Where? When? A grandmother in 1952, two students in a Neukölln kitchen…
The one scene from the story that people remember and repeat.
One detail on the packaging that shows the story: a date, a face, a map, a signature…
A few words that tell the whole story in one go.

values.founder: Morag, a fisherman’s wife on a very windy island off the west coast of Scotland, in 1952.
values.moment: The night of the big storm, when her porridge was so thick that the fishermen used it to fill a hole in their boat and got home safely. I am not saying this is true. I am saying I would buy it.
values.proof: A little wooden stick in every box, called a spurtle (that’s what Scots stir porridge with), and a drawing of Morag looking very unimpressed.
values.slogan: Thick enough to sail home on.

yours.label: Your brand
yours.heading: Your story
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your brand in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which story sells?
rank.placeholder: The brand, e.g. Granny Morag’s Storm Oats
